title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in this continuation of La Longue Marche (pp. 781–782), Grothendieck compares two local objects attached to a cusp/puncture x. The first is the small circle $_x around the puncture, with its universal coverings. The second is the punctured disc D_x^*, with its universal coverings. Both are viewed over a common abelian group T = T_x, the local fundamental (inertia) group. A_x is a category of 'admissible' objects (open sets A). Gr(A_x) is the groupoid obtained from it by inverting all arrows. The functors A ↦ $~_{x,A} and A ↦ D^{*~}_{x,A} induce equivalences F: Gr(A_x) → Revêtements($_x) and G: Gr(A_x) → Revêtements(D_x^*) (eq. 109). Choosing universal covers $~ and D^{*~} gives fibre functors A ↦ Isom(F(A), $~), which are T-torsors (eq. 110).

This page isolates the formal lemma behind that comparison. Data:
- three connected T-groupoids G, G', G''. These are connected groupoids in which every automorphism group is identified with the abelian group T, compatibly with conjugation; equivalently, gerbes over a point banded by T.
- T-equivalences F: G → G' and G: G → G''.
- objects X' ∈ G' and X'' ∈ G''.

Define f(X) = Hom_{G'}(F(X), X') and g(X) = Hom_{G''}(G(X), X''). These are functors G → Tors(T) (eq. 112). Form h(X) = Hom_{Tors(T)}(f(X), g(X)) = Isom_T(f(X), g(X)) (eq. 113).

Claim: h is a constant functor, i.e. canonically isomorphic to a constant T-torsor.

Proof: take quasi-inverses F_1: G' → G and G_1: G'' → G (eq. 114). Adjunction gives f(X) ≅ Hom_G(X, F_1(X')) and g(X) ≅ Hom_G(X, G_1(X'')) (eq. 115). Then Isom_T(Hom(X, Y'), Hom(X, Y'')) ≅ Hom_G(Y', Y''), via composition (eq. 116). The right-hand side is independent of X, whence the assertion.

Application: the T-torsor H(A) = Isom($~(A), D^{*~}(A)) does not depend on A. The next page uses this to define a 'corrélation' between a universal cover of the circle $_x and one of D_x^*: an element of this torsor. The correlations form a T_x-torsor, and the category Corr_x is equivalent to each category of universal covers. This is a careful bookkeeping of base points/tangential identifications at a puncture.
errors: Notational slip: (114) names the quasi-inverse of G as G_1, but (115)–(116) write F_2(X'') for it.

The proof as written leaves implicit that the identification Isom_T(Hom(X,Y'), Hom(X,Y'')) ≅ Hom(Y',Y'') uses commutativity of T and the T-groupoid compatibility; it also leaves implicit that the resulting isomorphism is natural in X, which is what 'constant' means. Both are routine and correct for abelian T.

ideas.what: T-groupoids (connected groupoids with all automorphism groups identified with an abelian group T compatibly), equivalences between them, and Hom-sets as T-torsors
ideas.modern_name: gerbes over a point banded by an abelian group T (T-gerbes); 2-category of banded gerbes
ideas.where_published: Idea of bands (liens) and gerbes underlies Giraud's book; this exact lemma not known in a published Grothendieck text

ideas.what: For T-equivalences out of a common T-groupoid, the torsor Isom(Hom(F X, X'), Hom(G X, X'')) is independent of X, equal to Hom(F_1 X', G_1 X'')
ideas.modern_name: Hom-torsors between objects of a banded gerbe; independence of base point for abelian band

ideas.what: Comparison ('corrélation') of universal covers of the boundary circle and of the punctured disc at a puncture, forming a T_x-torsor
ideas.modern_name: local monodromy / tangential base points at cusps
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (1989, 'Le groupe fondamental de la droite projective moins trois points') for tangential base points

deep.surprise_reason: The page proves a routine lemma about torsors in abelian-banded groupoids, as a technical step in the local base-point bookkeeping at punctures. There is nothing new beyond the well-known tangential-base-point philosophy.
transcription_corrections: First line: likely 'Gr(A_x)' and 'Revêtements($_x)', 'Revêtements(D_x^*)' rather than A_n / $_.
(113): the subscript under Hom is Tors(T) (written somewhat like 'Tors(J)').
(115)–(116): the manuscript indeed writes F_2(X'') although (114) introduced G_1; the transcription is faithful here.
'à priori on [?] dit que ce foncteur est est! constant': the sense is 'je dis que ce foncteur est constant'.
After (114), 'donc isomorphismes [?] fonctoriels en X' likely reads 'donc deux isomorphismes fonctoriels en X'.
